claims.text: The equiatomic FeNiCrMn alloy has a single-phase FCC initial structure.
The initial alloy has a random solute distribution.
The initial crystal contains no pre-existing vacancy clusters.
The initial crystal contains no pre-existing twin boundaries.
Yield strength is insensitive to strain rate from 10^8 to 10^10 s^-1.
Shockley partial dislocations nucleate from pre-existing solute-induced local lattice distortions rather than vacancy clusters.
Nucleation of the Shockley partials is thermally activated.
The <11-1> loading orientation has a higher maximum yield stress than the <110> orientation.
The higher yield stress of the <11-1> orientation results from a lower resolved-shear-stress factor on the primary {111}<112> slip system.
The HCP-like regions are stacking faults rather than a transformed phase.
Solute-induced local lattice distortions act as nucleation sites for Shockley partial dislocations.
Shockley partial dislocations generate intrinsic stacking faults with HCP-like local stacking.
Yielding begins through Shockley-partial nucleation from solute clusters having a reduced local critical resolved shear stress.
The lack of strain-rate sensitivity is caused by the dominance of athermal nucleation barriers at the simulated high strain rates.
Orientation dependence of yielding is governed by the Schmid factor of the active slip system.
Atoms in both FCC and true HCP environments have a local coordination number of 12.
Reversion of HCP-like regions to FCC stacking upon unloading would confirm that the regions are stacking faults.
A permanent ABAB stacking sequence after unloading would indicate a phase transformation rather than a stacking fault.

contradictions.description: Nucleation is described as thermally activated in the hypothesis but strain-rate insensitivity is attributed to dominant athermal nucleation barriers in the mechanism, without explaining how the thermal and athermal descriptions coexist.

The FCC initial state and true HCP are both described as having coordination number 12, yet the falsification rule says that the coordination number would 'drop to 12' during HCP transformation. Coordination number 12 alone therefore cannot provide the stated transition criterion.
